extracted.intended_audience: librarians, educators, authors, and publishers interested in the Newbery Award selection process
extracted.subtask_description: Description of the Newbery Award selection process: eligibility rules, the textual-quality focus and the specific evaluative dimensions considered by the ALA Children's Division panel, plus the panel composition and voting/scoring method that determine the Medal and Honor books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Given to the “most distinguished contribution to American literature for children.”

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary quality focus (textual quality)
rubrics_metrics.description: The book that is chosen is based on the quality of the text (not on book popularity or illustrations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection emphasizes literary/textual merit rather than popularity metrics or illustration quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any children's book published that year is eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The book must be published in the award year to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: place of first publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The book must be first published in America.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility: author residency/citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: The author must currently be a citizen or resident of the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot development
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot development (one of the judges' considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges evaluate the way the story unfolds and is structured over the course of the book.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of the central ideas or messages and how effectively they are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factual correctness where relevant (e.g., historical or informational content) and internal consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How clearly the text communicates its ideas and story to the intended child audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure and arrangement of material (chapters, pacing, coherence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality of concept, voice, perspective or treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character development
rubrics_metrics.description: Character development (one of the judges' considerations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depth, growth, and believability of characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectiveness and distinctiveness of place/time depiction and its role in the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriateness for children up to fourteen years old (Licciardo-Musso, 1999).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges consider whether content, themes, language, and presentation are suitable for children through age 14.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection panel composition and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Newbery Award winners are selected by librarians in the Children’s Division of the American Library Association; the Newbery panel consists of fifteen members who read a multitude of books throughout the year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel members read broadly through the year, discuss merits, and nominate contenders before voting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voting and scoring procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Each panel member picks three books – first choice gets four points, second choice gets three, and third choice gets two; the points are tallied and the winner is announced in January.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After deliberation and nomination, the point-based ballot determines the single Medal winner and up to six Honor books; the Medal winner receives a gold seal and Honor books receive silver seals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award guidance for educators
rubrics_metrics.description: Educators would benefit from familiarizing themselves with the Medal and Honor books.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the list of winners and honors as vetted, high-quality reading recommendations for children and curricula.
